correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives a single delayed 2x2 Jacobian. Its determinant reduces exactly to \(z^2+(1-k)z+(2-k)/3\) under \(z=s^q e^{s\tau}\). For \(-1<k\le0\) the discriminant is negative, the two conjugate roots have identical modulus, and explicit phase comparison proves which crossing is first. At \(k=-1/2\) the exact values \(\omega=0.908501523595597\ldots\) and \(\tau=1.147739992150082\ldots\) satisfy the original quasipolynomial, while \(\tau=1.0229\) does not. Implicit differentiation gives positive real crossing speed. The claim is restricted to this spectral fact and does not infer nonlinear Hopf properties.
